raw_response:
I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize rotation and only leave a smaller piece for cotton. I am 67, my household labor is limited, and some family labor is off-farm, so I will put most of my 16.1 mu into the system I know best and can manage steadily with machinery and well irrigation. I will use better seed on all crops because I have enough experience to judge input response and I do not want to waste land on weak stands. For wheat, I will push for a stable, medium-high yield with moderate fertilizer, two irrigations, and simple pest control. After wheat harvest, I will no-till maize on the same ground to save labor and keep the season tight. For cotton, I will keep only a smaller area because it takes more field attention and more pesticide work, but I will still manage it carefully with enough potassium and irrigation because I do not want it to drag down returns. Overall, I will choose a steady, labor-saving, risk-controlled plan rather than an aggressive one.
